summary: Built a 3-node MariaDB Galera cluster (node1, node2, node3) from scratch on CentOS Stream 10, populated it with application data (appdb.orders), then added node4 as a fourth member which received all existing data via SST (mariabackup) and now accepts writes that replicate to the other three members. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on all four nodes sequentially, preserving quorum throughout, with each node proven to have restarted (changed boot_id) and recovered full cluster membership, service health, and data integrity afterward.
actions_performed: Installed mariadb-server, mariadb-backup, galera, and mariadb-server-galera (for galera_new_cluster) on node1-node4
Populated /etc/hosts from CLUSTER_HOSTS, opened firewalld ports 3306/4567/4568/4444, and set SELinux boolean mysql_connect_any on all four nodes
Generated an SST auth password on node1 with openssl and distributed it to node2-4 over inter-node SSH (cluster keypair) rather than embedding literals in commands
Wrote /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf on node1-node3 with wsrep_cluster_address=gcomm://node1,node2,node3 and bootstrapped the cluster via galera_new_cluster on node1

Diagnosed and fixed an SST failure caused by an SELinux connectto denial on mariadb-backup's own mysqld_t socket by building and installing a minimal custom policy module (galera_sst.pp) via checkmodule/semodule_package/semodule on all four nodes
Started mariadb on node2 and node3, confirming they joined via SST/IST to reach wsrep_cluster_size=3, status Primary, Synced
Created appdb.orders table with seed rows on node1, created appuser with a node-generated random password, verified full replication and multi-writer inserts from node2 and node3
Updated wsrep_cluster_address on node1-3 to include node4 and wrote node4's own galera.cnf, then started mariadb on node4 which joined via SST to reach wsrep_cluster_size=4 carrying all existing data
Verified node4 accepts writes that replicate to node1, node2, and node3

Ran the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id + cluster health baseline on all four nodes, then restarted node1, node2, node3, and node4 one at a time (native reboot, backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect), polled each until reachable again, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified each node returned to wsrep_cluster_size=4, status Primary, Synced, with row_count intact before moving to the next node
Performed a final post-restart cross-node write from node4 and confirmed it replicated to node1

evidence.requirement: 3-node Galera cluster established on node1-3 with application data
evidence.summary: Shows no pre-existing cluster, then successful bootstrap on node1 (cluster_size=1, Primary, ready), growing to cluster_size=3/Primary/Synced after node2 and node3 joined, with appdb.orders seeded on node1

evidence.requirement: 3-node cluster accepts writes from any member (multi-writer)
evidence.summary: node2 and node3 already show replicated seed data; inserts issued from node2 (widget-D) and node3 (widget-E) both appear in node1's SELECT, proving multi-writer replication

evidence.requirement: node4 added as fourth member carrying existing data
evidence.summary: gcomm address updated on node1-3, node4 configured and started; node4 reaches wsrep_cluster_size=4/Primary/Synced and its SELECT shows all 5 pre-existing rows transferred via SST; node1 confirms cluster_size=4 with node4's address in wsrep_incoming_addresses

evidence.requirement: node4 accepts writes like other members and they replicate cluster-wide
evidence.summary: widget-F inserted on node4 appears in SELECT results on node1, node2, and node3

evidence.requirement: SELinux SST blocker root-caused and fixed with minimal reversible policy (supporting evidence for how the 3- and 4-node joins succeeded)
evidence.summary: mariabackup.backup.log showed a socket permission-denied error traced to an AVC connectto denial on mysqld_t; a custom semodule (galera_sst) was compiled and installed on all four nodes, after which SST succeeded

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/data
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 0581c914.../cluster_size=4/Synced/row_count=6; reboot ack returned; node unreachable confirming disruption; new boot_id 086ca6eb... proves restart; post-restart cluster_size=4/Primary/Synced and row_count=6 confirm recovery

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/data
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id be303eb3...; reboot ack returned; node unreachable; new boot_id 7b8b474e... proves restart; post-restart cluster_size=4/Primary/Synced and row_count=6 confirm recovery

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/data
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 96974ac3...; reboot ack returned; node unreachable; new boot_id 6c93e8ff... proves restart; post-restart cluster_size=4/Primary/Synced and row_count=6 confirm recovery

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/data
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 5e93a57c...; reboot ack returned; node unreachable; new boot_id 7543a60c... proves restart; post-restart cluster_size=4/Primary/Synced and row_count=6 confirm recovery; final cross-node write from node4 replicated to node1, proving the fully-restarted cluster remains a working multi-writer system
